title: Robot Barista Material Workshop
description: A robot barista stands behind a counter with a coffee mug. The user assigns and blends PBR materials across both objects using a coupled material-energy system: a fixed pool of 100 material-energy units must be conserved as you distribute metalness, roughness, emissive intensity, and opacity across the robot's body parts and the mug. Undo/redo lets you experiment freely while the energy budget always balances.
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that loads robot.glb and coffeeMug.glb via GLTFLoader. Place the robot behind a simple box-geometry counter and the mug on top of it. Use a PerspectiveCamera at (0,1.5,3.5) looking at (0,0.8,0), OrbitControls, an HDR-tone-mapped renderer, one DirectionalLight and one AmbientLight.

Implement a MATERIAL-ENERGY CONSERVATION SYSTEM: the scene has exactly 100 energy units total. The UI panel (HTML/CSS overlay on the left) lists 5 zones: Robot Head, Robot Torso, Robot Arms, Robot Legs, and Coffee Mug. Each zone shows four sliders: Metalness (0-1), Roughness (0-1), Emissive Intensity (0-3), and Opacity (0-1). Each slider tick costs energy proportional to its value (metalness*10, roughness*5, emissive*8, opacity*2 per zone). A top bar shows remaining energy. When a slider is dragged, if the total would exceed 100, clamp the slider. All material changes apply in real-time to the corresponding MeshStandardMaterial on the actual meshes (traverse the loaded models and group meshes by name/position into the 5 zones).

Implement MULTI-INPUT COUPLING: changing the mug's emissive intensity also tints the robot's torso emissive color to match (simulating reflected glow). Changing the robot head's metalness above 0.7 forces the mug's roughness to decrease by 0.1 (polished robot reflects onto mug).

Implement UNDO/REDO: every slider change pushes a snapshot of all 20 slider values onto a history stack. Buttons and Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z navigate history, restoring all materials and the energy counter. The history stack holds up to 30 states.

Add a 'Randomize' button that sets all sliders to random valid values respecting the 100-unit budget, counting as one undoable action. Display a step counter showing total interactions. Use at least 10-14 deliberate slider adjustments in the expected workflow to fully style both objects. Ensure all meshes start with default grey MeshStandardMaterial and energy at 100.
